A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Lyapunov-based SGDM study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v3.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C report original CIFAR-100/ResNet-18 experiments comparing scheduling strategies and optimizers.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix D report CIFAR-100 experiments and an additional ImageNet/ResNet-34 experiment.

M1.justification: Section 5.3 and Appendix E extend the analyzed NSHB procedure to non-increasing, time-varying momentum coefficients. The original SHB/NSHB algorithms and evaluated scheduling strategies remain; no specific dynamic-momentum schedule is experimentally evaluated.

E1.justification: V3 adds ImageNet evaluation alongside CIFAR-100, extending coverage within image classification. Appendix D.3 tests two already-used scheduling strategies on this additional benchmark.

E2.justification: The corresponding optimizer comparison retains SGD, NSHB, SHB-high, SHB-low, RMSProp, Adam, and AdamW. The ImageNet experiment compares existing schedules (ii) and (iv), introducing no new comparator.

E3.justification: RMSProp's reported learning rate changes from 0.01 to 0.0005, and Adam/AdamW change from 0.001 to 0.0005 (v2 Figure 3; v3 Figure 4). The added ImageNet experiment uses ResNet-34 for 200 epochs; the retained CIFAR-100 setup remains ResNet-18 for 300 epochs.

E4.justification: The four-schedule comparisons and learning-rate sensitivity sweeps are retained. ImageNet adds benchmark evidence, while the new discussions of sharp minima and dynamic momentum introduce no empirical ablation, robustness test, or mechanism analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report means over three runs with minimum–maximum shading. V3 introduces no new seed-reporting practice, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: The optimizer-comparison results are materially revised: v2's high RMSProp loss and gradient-norm plateaus are replaced by different trajectories under changed learning rates in v3 Figure 4. CIFAR appendix accuracy and gradient curves also change. New ImageNet Figure 17 reports lower final loss and gradient norm, and higher accuracy, for warmup schedule (iv) than schedule (ii); these are additional results, not cross-version performance gains.

T1.justification: V3 adds Theorem 3 and its proof for non-increasing momentum, including a modified Lyapunov coefficient and learning-rate condition; v2 discussed momentum scheduling only as future work. It also adds the dynamic-learning-rate residual derivation in Section 5.1 and corrects phase/geometric-sum indexing. Appendix A's SHB bound is retained mathematics separated from the original unified theorem.

C1.justification: The abstract qualifies the constant-batch convergence claim with 'under our Lyapunov-based analysis,' narrowing its scope. The central Lyapunov contribution, SHB/NSHB coverage, and claimed ordering of the four schedules remain.

C2.justification: V3 explicitly interprets the constant-batch variance floor as a limitation of its proof and explains the trade-off between proof simplicity and tighter variance control. It adds practical restrictions for large momentum, a noise-annealing interpretation involving sharp and flat minima, and a critical-batch-size rationale for the already-disclosed warmup synchronization mismatch.

D1.justification: The code-access reference changes from an anonymous 4open.science repository to an author-identified GitHub repository. V3 also supplies the ImageNet model and training duration and revises adaptive-optimizer learning-rate details; existing hardware, software, and CIFAR scheduling disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: V3 adds positioning against conditional-gradient batch scaling, diffusion-based analyses, and almost-sure SHB convergence, citing Islamov, Xie, and Sebbouh, among other additions. Table 1 changes Mai and Johansson's characterization from non-smooth convex to weakly convex. The central positioning relative to Liu, Kamo, and Umeda remains.

P1.justification: Much existing prose and the basic narrative progression remain. V3 makes localized explanatory rewrites, separates the SHB theorem into Appendix A, inserts a Discussion section, rewrites the conclusion, and updates terminology and author/contact text.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two-column to single-column layout, with substantially rearranged figures and a revised Table 1. Existing plots receive changed legends, insets, and presentation. V3 adds the overview schedule Figure 1 and ImageNet Figure 17; original Figures 1–15 otherwise correspond to Figures 2–16.

improvement.justification: V3 improves scientific precision by restricting the constant-batch claim to its analysis and explaining practical momentum limitations. The dynamic-momentum proof and ImageNet results provide useful extensions. The principal scheduling conclusions remain unchanged, and ImageNet tests only two schedules with limited setup detail, supporting a useful but limited overall improvement.
